title: The home-buying math just flipped

lines: The typical monthly payment on a new U.S. home —
the lowest in nearly two months.
Home prices have now fallen four weeks in a row,
after three years of only going up.
The hidden part: there are now over HALF A MILLION
more sellers than buyers across the country.
Redfin calls it the strongest buyer's market since 2013.
One in five listings has already cut its price.
When sellers outnumber buyers by half a million, the list price is a starting line, not the finish. Negotiate.
Would a lower payment get you off the sidelines?

source_line: Source: Redfin weekly housing-market update, 4 weeks ending Nov. 15, 2026 (published Nov. 19)
caption:
The typical monthly payment on a new U.S. home just fell to $2,723 — its lowest in nearly two months — and buyers suddenly hold the cards.

Redfin's latest weekly update (four weeks ending Nov. 15) shows the median U.S. home-sale price at $388,516, down 0.4% from a year ago — the fourth straight week of declines after three years of nonstop increases. The $2,723 payment, at a 7.11% average rate, is down from $2,760 a week earlier, though still 8.2% higher than last year.

The real shift: there are now over half a million more sellers than buyers nationwide — what Redfin calls the strongest buyer's market in its records going back to 2013. One in five listings (20.7%) has already cut its price.

My take: when sellers outnumber buyers by half a million, the list price is a starting line, not the finish. If you're shopping, ask for the discount — this market is built to give it.
